def-ahat-and-relative-chern-character-fo:
## Definition

Let $M$ be an oriented Riemannian manifold of dimension $2m$ and let $\Omega^{LC}$ be the skew-symmetric matrix of curvature two-forms of the Levi–Civita connection, with curvature convention
$R(X,Y)=[\nabla_X,\nabla_Y]-\nabla_{[X,Y]}$.
Define
$$\widehat A(TM,\nabla^{LC})=\det{}^{1/2}\!\left(\frac{i\Omega^{LC}/4\pi}{\sinh(i\Omega^{LC}/4\pi)}\right).$$
The determinant and square root are formal power series in commuting even-degree differential forms; the square-root branch has constant term $1$, and terms above degree $2m$ are discarded. This is the normalization of the A-hat characteristic form in [[def-chern-pontryagin-and-euler-characteristic-forms]].

For a graded Hermitian Clifford module $V$ with compatible connection, use the local multiplicity space and relative curvature from [[lem-spinor-and-clifford-associated-bundles-are-well-defined]]. Define the **relative Chern character form** by
$$
\operatorname{ch}(V/S)=\operatorname{str}_{W}\exp\!\left(-\frac{F^{V/S}}{2\pi i}\right).
$$
Here $\operatorname{str}$ is the ordinary trace if $W$ is ungraded and the even trace minus odd trace if it is graded. The cited well-definedness lemma proves this local expression patches to a global even form. For $V=S\widehat\otimes E$ with the product connection, it is $\operatorname{tr}\exp(-F^E/(2\pi i))$. The Chern–Weil supplier [[thm-chern-weil-forms-represent-the-at-characteristic-classes-over-the-reals]] identifies the resulting cohomology classes after passage to real coefficients; this definition asserts no integral torsion identity.
lem-good-cover-nerve-computes-singular-c:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold with a Riemannian metric, and let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\}_{i\in I}$ be an open cover whose members are strongly geodesically convex in the convention of [[thm-existence-of-geodesically-convex-neighborhoods]]. Let $N(\mathcal U)$ be the abstract simplicial complex whose finite nonempty subsets $\sigma\subset I$ are simplices exactly when $U_\sigma:=\bigcap_{i\in\sigma}U_i$ is nonempty. Then the geometric realization $|N(\mathcal U)|$ is homotopy equivalent to $M$. Writing $H^*_{\mathrm{simp}}(N;\mathbb F_2)$ for the cohomology of the simplicial cochain complex, the natural comparison identifies it with $H^*(M;\mathbb F_2)$.
def-graded-hermitian-clifford-module-and:
## Definition

Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold of even dimension $2m$, and let $V=V^+\oplus V^-$ be a finite-rank smooth complex vector bundle with a Hermitian metric linear in its first variable. Write $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathbb C}(T^*M,-g)$ for the complex Clifford bundle generated by cotangent vectors with relation $\xi\eta+\eta\xi=-2g^{-1}(\xi,\eta)$. A **graded Hermitian Clifford action** is a smooth real-linear map $c:T^*M\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ such that $c(\xi)^*=-c(\xi)$, $c(\xi)V^\pm\subseteq V^\mp$, and $c(\xi)c(\eta)+c(\eta)c(\xi)=-2g^{-1}(\xi,\eta)I$. It extends complex-linearly to the complex Clifford bundle.

A **graded Hermitian Clifford connection** is a unitary connection $\nabla^V$ preserving $V^\pm$ and satisfying
$$\nabla^V_X(c(\xi)v)=c(\nabla^{LC}_X\xi)v+c(\xi)\nabla^V_Xv$$
for smooth $X,\xi,v$, where $\nabla^{LC}$ is the Levi–Civita connection. In a local orthonormal coframe $(e^i)$ define
$$D_Vv=\sum_i c(e^i)\nabla^V_{e_i}v.$$
The operator is odd, so its chiral part is $D_V^+:C^\infty(V^+)\to C^\infty(V^-)$. The formula's frame independence, formal symmetry on closed $M$, and global bundle well-definedness are proved in [[lem-geometric-dirac-operator-is-well-defined]]. A domain and index are assigned only under the compact hypotheses of later items.
lem-geometric-dirac-operator-is-well-def:
## Statement

For a supplied graded Hermitian Clifford module and compatible connection as in [[def-graded-hermitian-clifford-module-and-geometric-dirac]], the local expression $D_V=\sum_i c(e^i)\nabla^V_{e_i}$ is independent of oriented orthonormal frame, is a smooth globally defined first-order differential operator, and is formally symmetric on a closed $M$.
lem-lichnerowicz-formula-for-geometric-d:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a Riemannian manifold and $V$ a graded Hermitian Clifford module with compatible connection as in [[def-graded-hermitian-clifford-module-and-geometric-dirac]]. Use $R(X,Y)=[\nabla^{LC}_X,\nabla^{LC}_Y]-\nabla^{LC}_{[X,Y]}$ and $\operatorname{Rm}(X,Y,Z,W)=g(R(X,Y)Z,W)$. In a local oriented orthonormal frame define
$$F^S_{ij}=\frac14\sum_{a,b}\operatorname{Rm}(e_i,e_j,e_a,e_b)c(e^a)c(e^b),\qquad F^{V/S}_{ij}=F^V_{ij}-F^S_{ij}.$$
Then $F^{V/S}_{ij}$ commutes with Clifford multiplication and
$$D_V^2=(\nabla^V)^*\nabla^V+\frac{\operatorname{scal}_g}{4}I+\sum_{i<j}c(e^i)c(e^j)F^{V/S}_{ij}.$$
In particular $D_V^2$ is formally symmetric Laplace type with positive-frequency principal symbol $|\xi|^2I$.
lem-dirac-maximal-domain-is-h1:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $M$ be closed, Riemannian, and of even dimension $n\ge2$. Let $D_V$ be the formally symmetric geometric Dirac operator of [[def-graded-hermitian-clifford-module-and-geometric-dirac]], and let $P=D_V^2$ have the Lichnerowicz form of [[lem-lichnerowicz-formula-for-geometric-dirac-operators]]. Then
$$\operatorname{dom}(\overline D_V)=H^1(M,V)=\{u\in L^2: D_Vu\in L^2\text{ distributionally}\},$$
its graph norm is equivalent to the $H^1$ norm, smooth sections are a core, and $\overline D_V$ is selfadjoint.
lem-chiral-dirac-is-fredholm-with-kernel:
## Statement

Assume full AC and the closed hypotheses of [[lem-dirac-maximal-domain-is-h1]]. The chiral operator
$$D_V^+:H^1(V^+)\longrightarrow L^2(V^-)$$
is Fredholm. Its kernel is $\ker D_V\cap L^2(V^+)$, its cokernel is canonically $\ker D_V\cap L^2(V^-)$, and
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}D_V^+=\dim\ker D_V^+-\dim\ker D_V^-.$$
Both kernels are finite-dimensional and consist of smooth sections.
lem-dirac-heat-trace-and-mckeen-singer-i:
## Statement

Assume full AC. For a closed even-dimensional manifold and a graded Hermitian geometric Clifford module, let $P=D_V^2$ with the $H^2$ selfadjoint domain. Its spectrum is discrete, nonnegative, of finite multiplicities, and has smooth eigensections. For $t>0$, $e^{-tP}$ is trace class and has a smooth kernel $K_t(x,y)$. The diagonal series and its derivatives converge uniformly for each $t>0$, and
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}D_V^+=\operatorname{Str}(e^{-tP})=\int_M\operatorname{str}K_t(x,x)\,d\operatorname{vol}_g(x),\qquad t>0.$$
lem-dirac-heat-parametrix-has-graph-norm:
## Statement

Assume full AC and the closed hypotheses of [[lem-dirac-heat-trace-and-mckeen-singer-index]]. In normal coordinates and radial parallel transport near the diagonal, let $h_t(x,y)=(4\pi t)^{-n/2}e^{-d(x,y)^2/(4t)}$ and define $u_0,u_1,\ldots$ by the heat-transport recursion below. After a cutoff supported inside the injectivity-radius neighborhood, for every $r,b,N\ge0$ there is $J$ such that the parametrix
$$H_J(t,x,y)=\chi(x,y)h_t(x,y)\sum_{j=0}^Jt^ju_j(x,y)$$
satisfies
$$\|K_t-H_J(t)\|_{C_x^rC_y^b}\le C_{r,b,N}t^N\quad(0<t\le1).$$
Thus the local heat expansion has a uniform differentiated remainder of arbitrary order; no convergence of rescaled global kernels is assumed.
def-spin-lift-of-oriented-orthonormal-fr:
## Definition

Let $E\to M$ be an oriented Euclidean real vector bundle of rank $n\ge1$. Its oriented frame bundle [[def-oriented-real-vector-bundle-and-oriented-frame-bundle]] has structure group $GL_n^+(\mathbb R)$, so the supplied metric gives an $SO(n)$ reduction: fiberwise Gram–Schmidt sends every oriented frame to an oriented orthonormal frame, and its formulas are smooth because each normalization divides by the positive norm of a nonzero orthogonal vector. Denote this principal right $SO(n)$-bundle by $P_{SO}(E)$.

For the positive Clifford convention $v^2=|v|^2$ and the full-even group of [[def-real-clifford-group-and-normalized-pin-spin]], write $\rho:\operatorname{Spin}_{\rm full}(n)\to SO(n)$ for the two-sheeted covering of [[thm-real-pin-spin-topological-double-covers]]. A **Spin lift** of $P_{SO}(E)$ is a right principal $\operatorname{Spin}_{\rm full}(n)$-bundle $P$ and a continuous map $\lambda:P\to P_{SO}(E)$ over $M$ satisfying $\lambda(ph)=\lambda(p)\rho(h)$. A Spin structure means an isomorphism class of such lifts over the identity of $P_{SO}(E)$. This definition concerns ranks $n\ge1$; the rank-zero Clifford convention is treated separately in the index theorem and is not assigned a torsor of unstabilized Spin structures.

The right-action convention is that of [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]].
def-even-dimensional-spinor-bundle-chira:
## Definition

Assume full AC. Let $M$ be an oriented Riemannian manifold of even dimension $n=2m\ge2$ with a specified Spin lift $P\to P_{SO}(TM)$. Let $S_0$ be the complex irreducible Clifford module of dimension $2^m$ supplied by [[thm-complex-spin-modules-and-compact-reducibility]], with positive-square complex Clifford action $c_+$ and full-even Spin representation $\sigma$. Put $c_0(v)=i\,c_+(v)$ for the negative-square cotangent action. This changes the Clifford square sign and preserves equivariance under $\sigma$, since the scalar $i$ commutes with that action. Define the complex spinor bundle by the associated real bundle $P\times_{\operatorname{Spin}(n)}(S_0)_{\mathbb R}$ using the realification of $\sigma$, and descend multiplication by $i$ and the Clifford action through their commuting transition maps.

For an oriented orthonormal basis $(e_1,\ldots,e_{2m})$, define the chirality operator on $S_0$ by $\Gamma_{S_0}=i^m c_0(e^1)\cdots c_0(e^{2m})$. The calculation below proves that this is basis-independent, squares to $1$, and anticommutes with each $c_0(\xi)$. Its $\pm1$ eigenspaces are $S_0^\pm$ and their associated bundles are $S^\pm$. The Levi–Civita connection on $P_{SO}(TM)$ lifts through the differential of $\operatorname{Spin}(n)\to SO(n)$ to the **spin connection** $\widetilde\nabla^S$ on $S$. This item defines these objects; [[lem-spinor-and-clifford-associated-bundles-are-well-defined]] supplies the global bundle, metric, connection, and transition verification.
lem-spin-structures-exist-iff-w2-vanishe:
## Statement

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $E\to M$ be an oriented Euclidean smooth real vector bundle of rank $n\ge1$ over a Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold. Then $E$ admits a Spin lift of [[def-spin-lift-of-oriented-orthonormal-frame-bundle]] if and only if $w_2(E)=0\in H^2(M;\mathbb F_2)$. When nonempty, isomorphism classes of lifts form a torsor under $H^1(M;\mathbb F_2)$: twisting a lift by a principal $\{\pm1\}$-bundle gives a free and transitive action. No distinguished lift is asserted. Rank zero is excluded.
lem-spinor-and-clifford-associated-bundl:
## Statement

Assume full AC. On an even-dimensional oriented Riemannian manifold with a supplied Spin lift, the realified associated construction in [[def-even-dimensional-spinor-bundle-chirality-and-spin-connection]] is a smooth Hermitian graded Clifford bundle with a global compatible spin connection. For any graded Hermitian Clifford module there is locally a graded factorization $V\cong S_0\widehat\otimes W$. Its local multiplicity spaces $W=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Cl}}(S_0,V)$ and the relative curvature $F^{V/S}:=F^V-c(R^{LC})$ have transition laws for which $\operatorname{str}_W\exp(-F^{V/S}/(2\pi i))$ is a global even form. In the spin-twisted case $V=S\widehat\otimes E$, this relative curvature is the curvature $F^E$ of the supplied unitary connection.
lem-getzler-radial-gauge-oscillator-lead:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Near any point $y$ of a closed even-dimensional geometric Clifford module, choose normal coordinates and radial parallel transport. Give $\partial_i$, $c(e^i)$, and $x^i$ Getzler degrees $1,1,-1$, respectively. The transport coefficients of [[lem-dirac-heat-parametrix-has-graph-norm-remainder]] have Getzler degree at most $2j$, and the leading operator of $D^2$ is the formal oscillator
$$P_0=-\sum_i\left(\partial_i+\frac14\sum_j\mathcal R_{ij}x^j\right)^2+F^{V/S}_y,$$
where $\mathcal R_{ij}=2F^S_{ji}(y)$ is the skew tangent-curvature matrix written in exterior-form symbols and $F^{V/S}$ is the relative twisting curvature. The diagonal supertrace coefficients vanish for $j<m$ when $n=2m$, and the $j=m$ coefficient is determined by the oscillator heat equation.
prop-positive-scalar-curvature-forces-un:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact boundaryless even-dimensional Spin Riemannian manifold, and suppose its scalar curvature satisfies $\operatorname{scal}_g(x)>0$ for every $x\in M$. Then every smooth untwisted spinor $\psi$ satisfying $D_S\psi=0$ is zero.
lem-mehler-supertrace-normalization-is-a:
## Statement

Assume full AC and the hypotheses of [[lem-getzler-radial-gauge-oscillator-leading-term]]. In the finite-dimensional even exterior-form algebra at $y$, the heat equation for $P_0$ has the normalized Gaussian solution
$$k_t(x,0)=(4\pi t)^{-m}\det^{1/2}\!\left(\frac{t\mathcal R/2}{\sinh(t\mathcal R/2)}\right)\exp\!\left(-\frac{1}{4t}x^T\bigl((t\mathcal R/2)\coth(t\mathcal R/2)\bigr)x\right)e^{-tF^{V/S}}.$$
The square root is the formal branch with constant term $1$. Its degree-$2m$ diagonal supertrace coefficient, with the curvature convention of [[def-ahat-and-relative-chern-character-forms]], is exactly $[\widehat A(TM,\nabla^{LC})\operatorname{ch}(V/S)]_{2m}$.
thm-geometric-clifford-module-dirac-inde:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact, boundaryless, oriented Riemannian manifold of even dimension $2m\ge2$, and let $V=V^+\oplus V^-$ be a finite-rank graded Hermitian Clifford module with compatible connection as in [[def-graded-hermitian-clifford-module-and-geometric-dirac]]. The chiral operator
$$D_V^+:H^1(M;V^+)\longrightarrow L^2(M;V^-)$$
is Fredholm and its complex index is
$$\operatorname{ind}(D_V^+)=\int_M\left[\widehat A(TM,\nabla^{LC})\operatorname{ch}(V/S)\right]_{2m}.$$
The integral is with the stated orientation. The result is a complex index; it makes no real KO-index assertion.
cor-spin-dirac-index-formula-with-arbitr:
## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $M$ be compact, boundaryless, oriented, Riemannian and Spin, of even dimension $2m\ge2$. Let $E\to M$ be any finite-rank complex Hermitian vector bundle with a unitary connection. Then the chiral Spin Dirac operator twisted by $E$ is Fredholm and
$$\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}(D^+_{S\otimes E})=\int_M\left[\widehat A(TM,\nabla^{LC})\operatorname{tr}\exp\!\left(-\frac{F^E}{2\pi i}\right)\right]_{2m}.$$
The rank-zero twist gives index and integral both equal to zero. This is a complex Fredholm index, not a real KO index.
cex-dirac-on-euclidean-space-is-not-fred:
## Statement

For $n\ge1$, let $S_0$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional Hermitian module for the negative-sign complex Clifford algebra, with skew-Hermitian generators $c(e^j)$ satisfying $c(\xi)^2=-|\xi|^2I$. On $\mathbb R^n$ with its Euclidean metric, let
$$D=\sum_{j=1}^n c(e^j)\partial_j,\qquad \operatorname{Dom}(D)=H^1(\mathbb R^n;S_0)\subset L^2(\mathbb R^n;S_0).$$
Then $D$ is closed and densely defined, its range is dense but not all of $L^2$, and therefore it is not Fredholm.
ex-complex-projective-plane-has-nonspin-:
## Statement

Let $x=c_1(\gamma^*)$ generate $H^2(\mathbb{CP}^2;\mathbb Z)$, where $\gamma$ is the tautological complex line. Then
$$w_2(T\mathbb{CP}^2)=\rho_2(c_1(T\mathbb{CP}^2))=\rho_2(3x)=\rho_2(x)\ne0.$$
Consequently the oriented tangent bundle of $\mathbb{CP}^2$ has no Spin lift.
ex-flat-even-torus-spin-dirac-has-index-:
## Statement

Assume full AC and dependent choice, with the complex spin-module suppliers in [A1]. On the flat torus
$T^{2m}=\mathbb R^{2m}/\mathbb Z^{2m}$ with the periodic Spin structure and $m\ge1$, the untwisted chiral Spin Dirac operator has index zero. Its kernel and adjoint kernel are precisely the constant positive- and negative-chirality spinors.
ex-positive-scalar-curvature-sphere-has-:
## Statement

Equip $S^2\cong\mathbb{CP}^1$ with its unit round metric and complex orientation. It has a Spin structure, its scalar curvature is $2$, and every smooth untwisted harmonic spinor is zero.
ex-twisted-sphere-dirac-index-and-curvat:
## Statement

Let $S^2$ have its unit round metric and complex orientation. Its tangent bundle admits a Spin lift; fix one. For each integer $k$, there is a Hermitian line bundle $L_k$ with unitary curvature
$$F^{L_k}=-2\pi i k\,\omega,\qquad \omega=\frac{\operatorname{area}_{S^2}}{4\pi},\quad \int_{S^2}\omega=1.$$
The twisted chiral Spin Dirac index is $k$. In an oriented orthonormal frame the twisting term in the Lichnerowicz formula is $-\frac{k}{2}\Gamma$, where $\Gamma=i\,c(e^1)c(e^2)$ is spinor chirality. Thus for $k\ne0$ the twist contributes a nonzero curvature endomorphism.
